subject: [hw] IV -> V16: valid T32 STRD with Rt2 != Rt+1 is UNDEF; vendor code executes it (0xE9C0 0x2100 at libvpud_vcodec+0x118ec)
body:
This is the first stop after V34s two missing shims, i.e. it blocks M-c on the vpud boot path.

Evidence (host, /tmp prototype; no tree writes): load the five vendor objects through V03 + V02 with the current tree, call apps_init (libvpud_vcodec 0x14269) or _app_venc_service->init (0x1101d) on a guest cpu:
  stop=UNDEF addr=400188ec insn=e9c02100  (libvpud_vcodec.so:venc_codec_service_init+0x4b, vaddr 0x118ec)
  another instance at libvpud_vcodec vaddr 0x8680 (0x4000f680 with base 0x40007000)
llvm-objdump --triple=thumbv7a-linux-gnueabi at 0x118ea..0x118f0:
  118ea: 6800    ldr r0, [r0]
  118ec: e9c0 2100  strd r2, r1, [r0]
  118f0: bd10    pop {r4, pc}
llvm-mc --show-encoding agrees: "ldrd r2, r1, [r0]" -> [0xd0,0xe9,0x00,0x21]. So the word is a well-formed T32 STRD T1 with Rt=2, Rt2=1 (Rt2 = Rt-1), not a misdecode: n2a32_t32_mem() routes it to dual_excl() and your documented rule (emu/n2a32_t32_mem.c, comment lines 45-46: "an encoded Rt2 != Rt + 1" -> UNDEF) rejects it.

Why the rule is wrong for this target: the Rt2 == Rt+1 requirement is the ARMv7 A32 LDRD/STRD constraint; the T32 encodings and ARMv8-A AArch32 allow any Rt2 != Rt != 15 (the vendor library is built for cortex-a55, Tag_CPU_arch v8-A, per FACTS 1.23). The compiler emitted exactly that form, and Android ran it on this SoC.

Request: accept Rt2 != Rt (and Rt != Rt2, neither 15) for T32 LDRD/STRD, both the immediate and literal forms, and add a case with 0xE9C0 0x2100 (strd r2,r1,[r0]) plus its LDRD twin. FACTS 4.8 census: strd 3084, ldrd 1174, so the count matters. Answer on the board when fixed; I re-run the vendor boot and pass the next stop back, or post DONE IV with M-b or further.
